'''Kathryn Ann Whitehead''' (born 1980) is an American chemical engineer who is a professor at [[Carnegie Mellon University]]. Her research focuses on the engineering of [[Nanomaterials|nanomaterial]]-based drug delivery systems for [[gene therapy]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Kathryn Whitehead: mRNA offers potential new treatment for pancreatic diseases| website=[[YouTube]] | date=29 March 2023 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SFVexFLRmTc |access-date=3 May 2023}}</ref> oral macromolecular delivery systems,<ref>{{cite web |title=Katie Whitehead: Advanced Nanoparticle Research for Drug Delivery | date=2 July 2014 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ejaqK0WM_34 |publisher=Carnegie Mellon University |access-date=3 May 2023}}</ref> and maternal and infant therapeutics.<ref>{{cite web |title=carnegie mellon kathryn whitehead - YouTube | date=4 October 2018 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=69_zjOaknoA |publisher=Carnegie Mellon University |access-date=3 May 2023}}</ref> She was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering]] in 2021<ref>{{cite web |title= Kathryn Whitehead, Ph.D. COF-6152 - AIMBE |url=https://aimbe.org/college-of-fellows/cof-6152/ |publisher=AIMBE |access-date=3 May 2023}}</ref> and as Fellow of the Controlled Release Society.<ref>{{cite web |title= College of Fellows Award Recipients |url=https://www.controlledreleasesociety.org/college-fellows-award-recipients |access-date=3 May 2023}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Whitehead is from [[Allentown, Pennsylvania]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Kathryn Whitehead |url=https://engineering.cmu.edu/directory/bios/whitehead-kathryn.html |access-date=2022-09-04 |website=engineering.cmu.edu |language=en}}</ref> She earned her bachelor's degree in [[chemical engineering]] at the [[University of Delaware]],<ref name=":0" /> then moved to the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]], where she studied methods to improve the oral delivery of [[macromolecule]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Whitehead |first=Kathryn Ann |date=2007 |title=Safe and effective methods for improving the oral delivery of macromolecules |url=https://worldcat.org/en/title/759567167 |access-date=2022-09-04 |website=worldcat.org}}</ref> Whitehead was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[Koch Institute for Integrative Cancer Research]], where she worked alongside [[Robert S. Langer]] on [[RNA interference]] therapeutics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kathryn A. Whitehead - Biomedical Engineering |url=https://www.cmu.edu/bme/People/Faculty/profile/kwhitehead.html |access-date=3 May 2023}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Whitehead's research included the development of drug delivery systems for gene therapies.<ref>{{Citation |title=Katie Whitehead: Advanced Nanoparticle Research for Drug Delivery | date=2 July 2014 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ejaqK0WM_34 |language=en |access-date=2022-09-04}}</ref> She is interested in the development of nanoparticle materials to deliver [[messenger RNA]] (mRNA) to specific cells.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Kathryn Whitehead: How can we safely deliver vaccines to the right cells? |language=en |work=NPR.org |url=https://www.npr.org/2021/10/29/1050313178/kathryn-whitehead-how-can-we-safely-deliver-vaccines-to-the-right-cells |access-date=2022-09-04}}</ref> Targeted mRNA delivery provides physicians with a personalized strategy to treat genetic disorders.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=University |first=Carnegie Mellon |date= |title=Whitehead Wins DARPA Young Faculty Award - News - Carnegie Mellon University |url=http://www.cmu.edu/news/stories/archives/2016/november/whitehead-darpa-award.html |access-date=2022-09-04 |website=www.cmu.edu |language=en}}</ref> Alongside mRNA, Whitehead has studied [[small interfering RNA]], which can be used to control [[gene expression]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Kathryn Whitehead |url=https://www.technologyreview.com/innovator/kathryn-whitehead/ |access-date=2022-09-04 |website=MIT Technology Review |language=en}}</ref> In general, mRNA promotes gene expression, whilst siRNA is used to silence over-expressed genes.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=University |first=Carnegie Mellon |date= |title=Whitehead's Research Could Revolutionize Medicine with Cutting-Edge Science - News - Carnegie Mellon University |url=http://www.cmu.edu/news/stories/archives/2018/july/whitehead-research.html |access-date=2022-09-04 |website=www.cmu.edu |language=en}}</ref> She focuses on the development of delivery systems for [[leukocytes]] (including [[B cell]]s) and [[intestinal epithelium]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Pittsburgh |first1=A. Carnegie Mellon University Publication 5000 Forbes Avenue |last2=Pa 15213268-2000 |title=What if... |url=http://cmtoday.cmu.edu/science_innovation/cancer-treatment-innovative-research/ |access-date=2022-09-04 |website=Carnegie Mellon Today |language=en}}</ref> A challenge with using mRNA for therapeutic purposes is that the body often recognizes foreign mRNA and attacks it, triggering an immune response.<ref name=":3" /> She worked with [[Katalin Karikó]] and [[Drew Weissman]] on the development of the lipid nanoparticles that enabled the mRNA-based [[COVID-19 vaccine]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smedley |first=Tim |title=Could mRNA make us superhuman? |url=https://www.bbc.com/future/article/20211122-could-mrna-make-us-superhuman |access-date=2022-09-04 |website=www.bbc.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Without these lipid shells, there would be no mRNA vaccines |url=https://cen.acs.org/pharmaceuticals/drug-delivery/Without-lipid-shells-mRNA-vaccines/99/i8 |access-date=2022-09-04 |website=cen.acs.org}}</ref>

In an attempt to better design drug delivery systems, Whitehead has investigated the cellular components of [[breast milk]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=University |first=Carnegie Mellon |date= 6 July 2022|title=Mother's Milk Cells Key to Novel Infant Disease Therapy - News - Carnegie Mellon University |url=http://www.cmu.edu/news/stories/archives/2022/july/breast-milk-disease-therapy.html |access-date=2022-09-04 |website=www.cmu.edu |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Gleeson |first1=John P. |last2=Chaudhary |first2=Namit |last3=Fein |first3=Katherine C. |last4=Doerfler |first4=Rose |last5=Hredzak-Showalter |first5=Patricia |last6=Whitehead |first6=Kathryn A. |date=July 2022 |title=Profiling of mature-stage human breast milk cells identifies six unique lactocyte subpopulations |journal=Science Advances |language=en |volume=8 |issue=26 |article-number=eabm6865 |doi=10.1126/sciadv.abm6865 |issn=2375-2548 |pmc=9242445 |pmid=35767604|bibcode=2022SciA....8M6865G }}</ref> She is interested in whether it is possible to genetically engineer cells to treat children's allergies, or orally administer vaccines to infants.<ref name=":4" />

Whitehead is passionate about science communication and improving public trust in science.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/pittsburgh/news/2022/01/30/personalities-of-pittsburgh-dr-kathryn-whitehead.html | title=Personalities of Pittsburgh: Dr. Kathryn Whitehead is on the cutting edge of vaccine development |access-date=2022-09-04 |website=www.bizjournals.com}}</ref> In 2021, she delivered a [[TED (conference)|TED]] talk on lipid nanoparticles and how mRNA will transform biology.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Whitehead |first=Kathryn A. |title=Kathryn A. Whitehead {{!}} Speaker {{!}} TED |url=https://www.ted.com/speakers/kathryn_a_whitehead |access-date=2022-09-04 |website=www.ted.com |language=en}}</ref> In 2022, Whitehead delivered the [[convocation]] address at the [[Carnegie Mellon University]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=University |first=Carnegie Mellon |date= 26 August 2022|title=Convocation Inspires New Class - News - Carnegie Mellon University |url=http://www.cmu.edu/news/stories/archives/2022/august/convocation.html |access-date=2022-09-04 |website=www.cmu.edu |language=en}}</ref>
